Thanks to a new partnership with RapidSOS, emergency service departments in Brazil can now request real-time video streaming from iPhone users. Details below.

Emergency SOS Live Video Feature Expands to Brazil

Not everyone may know that one of the iPhone's many emergency features is the ability to share real-time video with emergency services during a call.

Here is Apple's description of this feature:

Share live video or existing photos with emergency services (not available in all countries or regions). If requested by emergency services, you can use "Emergency SOS Live Video" to stream live video or upload existing photos and videos to emergency services.

Apple notes that emergency services can retain a copy of shared videos, and users can choose whether to accept requests to share video or photos. Apple also states that "Emergency SOS Live Video" is available on iPhone 14 or later models, and is subject to device limitations and may not be available in certain situations.

That said, RapidSOS, a public safety AI company, announced today that Apple's "Emergency SOS Live Video" feature is now available to emergency communications centres (ECCs) across Brazil, allowing iPhone users to "safely share live video at the request of 190 during emergencies".

190 is the Brazilian equivalent of 911.

RapidSOS notes that this is the same technology first enabled for US emergency services with the launch of iOS 18 in September 2024, and lists three key features of this integration:

Simple and secure operation: During an emergency call, if the dispatcher believes video would help handle the situation, they can send a request to the caller's device. The caller sees a prompt and can share a live video stream from their camera with a single tap. The feature is encrypted by default, and the caller can stop sharing at any time.

Michael Martin, founder and CEO of RapidSOS, commented on today's announcement: "RapidSOS is honoured to be the first platform in the United States to enable this feature," and added that the company is "committed to bringing this same life-saving technology to emergency services around the world".
